name: Akhnoor Fort
coordinates_source: District Administration Jammu, National Informatics Centre official map direction
description: An imposing two-tiered historical fort perched on a cliff overlooking the Chenab River, celebrated for ancient Harappan excavations and its sacred riverfront coronation ghat.
historical_background: Initiated in 1762 by Raja Tegh Singh and completed in 1802 by Raja Alam Singh, this ASI-protected monument marks the historic coronation site of Maharaja Gulab Singh at Jia Pota Ghat.

name: Amar Mahal Jammu
coordinates_source: District Administration Jammu, National Informatics Centre official map direction
description: A 19th-century palace built in a French-chateau style, now a museum with miniature paintings and manuscripts.
historical_background: Commissioned by Raja Amar Singh and designed by a French architect in the style of a French chateau, the palace was planned in 1862 though actually built in the 1890s. It later served as the last official residence of the Dogra dynasty. Converted into a museum in 1975 (inaugurated by then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi), it now houses a 120 kg gold throne, Pahari and Kangra miniature paintings, and a library of roughly 25,000 antique books.

name: Bagh-e-Bahu
coordinates_source: District Administration Jammu, National Informatics Centre official map direction
description: A historic Dogra-era fort with a garden overlooking the Tawi river — a good sunset stop.
historical_background: Believed to be the oldest structure in Jammu, with origins traced back roughly 3,000 years to Raja Bahulochan, said to be the brother of Jammu's founder. The fort was rebuilt and expanded multiple times over the centuries, with its current form largely shaped by Maharaja Gulab Singh in the 19th century. It houses a Kali temple known locally as Bawey Wali Mata, and overlooks the terraced Mughal-style Bagh-e-Bahu gardens below.

name: Raghunath Temple Jammu
coordinates_source: District Administration Jammu, National Informatics Centre official map direction
description: One of North India's largest temple complexes, in the heart of Jammu city.
historical_background: Construction began in 1835 under Maharaja Gulab Singh, founder of the Dogra dynasty, and was completed by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh by 1860. The complex holds seven interconnected shrines, each with its own shikhara (spire), and is considered one of the largest temple complexes in North India. Its main deity is Lord Rama (Raghunath).

coordinates_source: District Administration Srinagar, National Informatics Centre official map direction

name: Dachigam National Park
coordinates_source: District Administration Srinagar, National Informatics Centre official map direction
description: A pristine high-altitude wildlife sanctuary spanning Himalayan temperate forests, recognized as the last refuge of the critically endangered Hangul (Kashmir stag).
historical_background: Originally created as a protected royal game preserve by the Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir to supply clean drinking water to Srinagar, designated a National Park in 1981.

coordinates_source: District Administration Kishtwar, National Informatics Centre official map direction

historical_background: Notified in 1981 to conserve the fragile high-altitude ecosystem and biodiversity of the upper Catchment of the Chenab River basin in the Greater Himalayas.
